title: Taking bands to the Dixieland Jubilee and Pete Fountain's break
summary: Mares took New Orleans bands to the West Coast Dixieland Jubilee in 1954 and 1956; Fountain was noticed by Lawrence Welk's son there.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Jubilee. I was going to ask about those trips that you made out there too.

Well, I brought Al Hoyt and I brought little Warren Luling and Pete Fountain. And I engineered that job because they never had Hoyt any other boys that I brought out there. And I told Pete at that time, I said, Pete, you're playing a lot of clarinet and maybe if the right people would hear you, maybe you'd get a break. And it's exactly what happened. Lawrence Welk's boy happened to be in the audience. He told his daddy he heard a terrific clarinet player. We gave Pete his tunes, Tin Roof Blues and the March of the Bobcats and the Jazz Me Blues, which he, was his crib numbers, which he does very, very good. We put a sub mic up there and Pete knocked him out. Well, the rest is history with Pete. He finally went with Lawrence Welk. And today Pete's a big name.
What was the first year you went out there?

Well, in 1954, Frank Bullas wrote down here in New Orleans and asked me to get a bunch together. And I brought Raymond Boyk, Jack Delaney, Johnny St. Cyr and little Georgie Girard. And we competed that year with eight bands and we came out on top.
That's on the record, by the way. The Gene Norman Presents record is still available.

It's still available. But we really laid him in the aisle and it gave those boys a nice break. It gave Georgie Girard a good break. And like I say, George could have went on to big and better things if Miss Fortune wouldn't have took him and passed away. But I get a kick out of trying to help a few of the boys. If I can do anything to give them just a little bit of help. Like I said, Bill, Dixieland's in my heart. I love it. I guess I always will. And I like the music and I like the boys. And if I can help them anyway and I'll keep on plugging. I'll keep on making Southlands. And like I say, you never know who's going to hear you. And some of them might get a break out of it. There's quite a few boys like little Dutch Andrews and them that got their first recording date with me. I recorded quite a bit of the names. Tony Peretti and Georgie Brunas. I finally got Georgie on my label. And I have quite a few of the real boys.
